mutation in the gene BRCA1 and explain why this mutation would put the person at a greater
risk of breast cancer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:

occurs, the DNA sample goes through the polymerase chain reaction (PCR).

• 1 in 400 females have a mutated allele of BRCA1

they are 80 years old.
In 2022, the population of females in the UK was 3.5 × 10 .

breast cancer by the age of 80 years old. Give your answer in standard form.

text: The gene BRCA1 is expressed in breast tissue and in several other tissues of the body. BRCA1
codes for a tumour suppressor protein. This protein is involved in either repairing damaged DNA,
or in triggering the death of a cell if DNA cannot be repaired.
Some mutations in BRCA1 are associated with an increased risk of developing breast cancer.
